content: Alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase ALG2 is an enzyme encoded by the ALG2 gene in humans. Mutations in the ALG2 gene are linked to congenital glycosylation defects. This gene produces a protein that belongs to the glycosyltransferase 1 family. The protein functions as an alpha-1,3-mannosyltransferase, which catalyzes the addition of mannose residues to specific dolichol-linked oligosaccharides. Specifically, it transfers mannose to Man(2)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate and Man(1)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate, resulting in the formation of Man(3)GlcNAc(2)-dolichol diphosphate. Mutations or defects in this gene are associated with congenital disorder of glycosylation type Ih (CDG-Ih), a condition that disrupts normal glycosylation processes. The ALG2 protein has been demonstrated to interact with annexin A7 (ANXA7) and annexin A11 (ANXA11), which are proteins involved in various cellular processes, including membrane trafficking and calcium signaling.
